## Your Child Benefit Eligibility Assessment

Based on my review of the official UK government guidance, here's your eligibility status:

### **✓ ELIGIBLE for Alex (17 years old)**
You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex because:
- Alex is 17 and in approved education
- The rules allow Child Benefit to continue for children under 20 if they stay in approved education or training
- Alex lives with you in the UK and meets all other requirements

### **✗ INELIGIBLE for Blake (18 years old)**
You are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Blake because:
- Blake is 18 and **not** in approved education or training
- Child Benefit for children over 16 only continues if they stay in approved education or training
- Blake doesn't qualify for the 20-week extension period (which only applies to 16-17 year olds who have recently left education and registered with careers services)

### Summary
**You can claim Child Benefit for Alex only.** You should apply for Child Benefit for Alex if you haven't already done so. If you were previously receiving Child Benefit for Blake, those payments should have stopped when Blake turned 16 (if not in education) or when they left approved education.

**Important note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge.

reasonings: Alex is 17 years old and in approved education. Alex meets these criteria: (1) is under 20 years old, (2) is in approved education, (3) lives with you in the UK, (4) is not in local authority care, (5) is not in hospital or residential accommodation, (6) is not fostered, (7) does not work 24+ hours/week, (8) has not started an apprenticeship in England, and (9) does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right. Therefore, you are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.

Blake is 18 years old and NOT in approved education or training, and is not in the extension period. The eligibility rules state that you'll normally still qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 AND they stay in approved education or training. Additionally, the rules specify you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child 'is no longer in approved education or training.' Since Blake is 18 and not in approved education or the 20-week extension period (which applies only to 16 or 17 year olds who have left education/training and registered with a careers service or armed services), Blake does not meet the criteria for continued Child Benefit beyond age 16. Therefore, you are INELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Blake.
